text:
acme-sre: Hey, getting intermittent 504s when our service cancels request contexts — Go SDK v1.3.2. Happens when we abort on user nav. Quick repro below. Anyone seen this?

alex: Can you paste the tiny repro and logs? Also, are you using a custom http.Client/Transport?

acme-sre: Repro (simplified):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, \"POST\", apiURL, bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
resp, err := redwoodClient.HTTPClient.Do(req) // redwoodClient.HTTPClient is the SDK's http.Client
if err != nil { log.Printf(\"err=%v\", err); return }
// sometimes we never get here, we see 504 from edge
```
We see the client return context canceled locally but the Redwood API logs show a request handled and timed out (504). Feels like a retry landed on the server after we cancelled.

maria: Two quick things to check: 1) Does the SDK call `req.WithContext` everywhere? 2) Are you using a retry policy that can requeue a request after ctx cancel?

acme-sre: We're using default SDK config. We did override Transport settings:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0} // timeout via ctx
redwoodClient.HTTPClient = client
```

sam: If the higher-level SDK retry layer isn't checking ctx.Err() after a send error, it may re-enqueue. Also, Go's transport can return an error to the caller while a connection still transmits on the wire (rare), causing the server to receive a request after client-side cancel.

alex: Can you share the server-side request IDs from the logs? That will show if duplicate requests are reaching the backend after cancel. Also include `X-Request-Id` header from the SDK (should be on the request).

acme-sre: Attached snippet from logs: server shows request-id r-9a8b7c got a long handler and then 504. Client logs show ctx canceled then later sdk retry attempted.

maria: There's a known issue in SDK v1.3.2 where the retry middleware will treat certain transport errors (net/http ErrClosedPipe / EOF) as retriable even if ctx was canceled; fixed in v1.4.0 to check ctx err before retry. Two options: upgrade to v1.4.0 or patch locally by setting a short ResponseHeaderTimeout on Transport to avoid long server hang.

sam: Repro test we use at Redwood: run a toy server that sleeps 200ms, client context 50ms, SDK retry enabled. With v1.3.2 you can see a second attempt fired after cancel. Example server: 
```go
http.HandleFunc(\"/sleep\", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request){
  time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
  w.WriteHeader(200)
})
http.ListenAndServe(\":8080\", nil)
```
Client: make request with ctx timeout 50ms and observe server logs for duplicate hit.

acme-sre: OK we'll test upgrade path. If we can't upgrade right away, is there a safe transport-level work-around?

maria: Workarounds: 
- Set Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout to something like 3s so hung backends don't linger.
- Consider DisableKeepAlives = true if you suspect connection reuse is causing unexpected behavior (tradeoff: more TLS handshakes).
- As a last resort, set SDK retry policy to disable retries for idempotency=false requests or on context.Canceled errors.

alex: Also ensure you always use `req = req.WithContext(ctx)` before any retries or signing middleware. If middleware wraps the request and loses the ctx, cancel won't propagate.

eng-oncall: Filed INC-3859 to track a customer-facing KB + backport patch to v1.3.x branch for a guard that checks `if ctx.Err() != nil { return ctx.Err() }` before retrying.

acme-sre: Thanks — upgrading to v1.4.0 + setting ResponseHeaderTimeout fixed our repro. No duplicate hits observed. We'll monitor production and reopen if it reappears. :thumbsup:

sdk-bot: Note: release v1.4.0 includes fix: \"do not retry if request context is canceled\" and a new opt-in RetryOnNetworkOnly policy. See changelog: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/releases/tag/v1.4.0

maria: Great — ping us if you still see anything.

acme-sre: Will do, thanks everyone!
